title: Draft: radius: update Ingate Systems AB RADIUS dictionary to use uint32

notes.body:
The FreeRADIUS commit from two weeks ago changed *all* dictionaries, not just one.

In RFC 2865, "integer" is clearly defined as meaning a 32 bit unsigned integer. (https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2865#section-5)

The official IANA assignment lists continue to use "integer" for this meaning: https://www.iana.org/assignments/radius-types/radius-types.xhtml

It is not clear that the Wireshark RADIUS dictionary parser in `radius_dict.l` supports using "uint32" - in fact, there is a comment towards the top:

```
 * XXX - features not currently supported:
 *
 *      integer64, ipv4prefix, combo-prefix, bool, size, decimal,
 *      timeval, struct, extended, long-extended, vsa, evs, vendor,
 *      cidr, uint{8,16,32,64}, int{8,16,32,64} as attribute types
 *      (some of these aren't documented);
```

Did you test this MR with the changed type names?

There are decent arguments for changing the name, and for trying to remain compatible with FreeRADIUS dictionaries, but not as this MR stands.
Agreed. I'll get back to you on this.
At present, this does not look like a good addition. Closing. Can re-open if the situation changes.
Probably the first step is making our RADIUS dictionary processing handle these types.
